title: The Birth of Lord Rama
story: King Dasharatha of Ayodhya longs for a son and performs a sacred yajna. A divine offering is given to his queens, and in time Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana and Shatrughna are born.

title: The Arrival of Sage Vishwamitra
story: Sage Vishwamitra arrives at King Dasharatha's court and asks that Rama accompany him to protect his sacred yajna.

title: Rama Protects the Yajna
story: Rama and Lakshmana travel with Vishwamitra and protect his sacred yajna from forces that seek to disturb it.

title: Sita's Swayamvara
story: In Mithila, King Janaka announces a great challenge for Sita's swayamvara. Princes from many kingdoms gather to attempt it.

title: Rama Breaks Shiva's Bow
story: Rama approaches the mighty bow of Shiva. With divine strength, he lifts the bow and breaks it, astonishing everyone present.

title: Rama and Sita's Wedding
story: After Rama succeeds at the swayamvara, preparations begin for the wedding of Rama and Sita, bringing joy to Mithila and Ayodhya.

title: Kaikeyi's Two Boons
story: Queen Kaikeyi remembers two promises granted by Dasharatha. She asks that Bharata become king and Rama be sent into exile for fourteen years.

title: Rama Accepts Exile
story: Rama learns that he must leave Ayodhya for fourteen years. Instead of anger, he accepts the decision to protect his father's honor.

title: Sita Chooses to Follow Rama
story: Sita refuses to remain in Ayodhya while Rama lives in the forest. She chooses to accompany her husband despite the hardships ahead.

title: Lakshmana Joins Rama
story: Lakshmana decides that he cannot let Rama and Sita face the forest alone. He leaves Ayodhya with them and begins their journey.

title: Rama Leaves Ayodhya for the Forest
story: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana set out for the forest in Sumantra's chariot. The whole city follows them in tears, and the people of Ayodhya beg Rama not to go, but he gently stays true to his father's word.

title: Guha the Boatman Ferries Rama Across the Ganga
story: At the banks of the Ganga, Guha, the king of the Nishadas, welcomes Rama with deep love and offers him everything. Rama sends Sumantra back to Ayodhya, and Guha ferries Rama, Sita and Lakshmana across the great river.

title: The Death of King Dasharatha
story: Upon Sumantra's return to Ayodhya with the empty chariot, King Dasharatha is consumed by overwhelming grief for his exiled son. Recalling a tragic curse from his youth involving the dutiful Shravana Kumar, the heartbroken monarch breathes his last breath. Ayodhya is plunged into deep mourning, left leaderless without its king or its beloved prince.

title: Bharata Rejects the Throne
story: Summoned back to Ayodhya from his uncle's kingdom, Prince Bharata arrives to find the city submerged in sorrow and learns of King Dasharatha's death and Rama's exile. Devastated and enraged by his mother Kaikeyi's deceitful actions, Bharata fiercely rejects the kingdom offered to him. He vows to travel into the forest to bring his beloved brother Rama back to take his rightful place on the throne.

title: Bharata's Journey to Chitrakoot
story: Determined to bring Rama back to Ayodhya, Bharata sets out into the forest accompanied by the royal mothers, ministers, and a vast procession of citizens. Along the way, he meets the forest chieftain Guha, who realizes Bharata's selfless devotion and assists the procession in crossing the holy Ganges River toward Chitrakoot.

title: Bharata Meets Rama at Chitrakoot
story: Upon reaching Chitrakoot, Bharata rushes to Rama's humble hermitage and falls weeping at his elder brother's feet. Deeply moved, Rama embraces Bharata, only to be struck with grief upon learning the tragic news of King Dasharatha's passing. Together with Lakshmana and Sita, the brothers offer sacred rites and mourn the loss of their beloved father in the forest.

title: Bharata Receives Rama's Sandals
story: Bharata earnestly begs Rama to return to Ayodhya and claim his rightful throne, but Rama steadfastly refuses to break their late father's sacred vow. Accepting Rama's resolve, Bharata requests his elder brother's wooden sandals to place upon the throne as a symbol of Rama's ultimate sovereignty. Bharata vows to live as an ascetic in Nandigram and rule Ayodhya only as a humble regent until Rama completes his fourteen-year exile.

title: The Blessing of Sage Atri and Anasuya
story: Following Bharata's departure, Rama decides to leave Chitrakoot to seek deeper solitude and protect the forest sages from disturbing forces. Journeying deeper into the wilderness, the royal trio arrives at the peaceful ashram of the venerable Sage Atri and his pious wife, Anasuya. Anasuya warmly receives Sita, imparting sacred wisdom on devotion and bestowing upon her celestial garments and ornaments that will never fade.

title: Encounter with Viradha in Dandakaranya
story: Leaving Sage Atri's peaceful hermitage, Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana venture into the dense and treacherous Dandakaranya forest. They are soon ambushed by the fearsome demon Viradha, who attempts to seize Sita and overpower the brothers. Rama and Lakshmana defeat the formidable rakshasa, liberating his soul and marking their first major triumph over evil in the wilderness.

title: Sage Sharabhanga's Ascendance and Rama's Sacred Vow
story: Following the encounter with Viradha, Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana arrive at the hermitage of Sage Sharabhanga, where they witness Lord Indra departing after visiting the holy ascetic. Having waited to behold Rama before relinquishing his earthly form, Sage Sharabhanga enters the sacred fire and ascends to heaven. Moved by the sight of sages' bones slain by rakshasas, Rama solemnly vows to protect the hermits and eliminate evil from Dandakaranya.

title: Visit to Sage Sutikshna's Hermitage
story: Continuing their journey through Dandakaranya, Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita arrive at the peaceful ashram of Sage Sutikshna. The pious sage warmly welcomes the royal trio and offers them his hospitality and spiritual blessings. During their stay, Sita gently questions the necessity of bearing arms in the forest, allowing Rama to reaffirm his sacred commitment to protect the sages.

title: Meeting Sage Agastya and Receiving Divine Weapons
story: After spending nearly ten years visiting various hermitages in Dandakaranya, Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita journey to the sacred ashram of the venerated Sage Agastya. The great sage warmly welcomes them and bestows upon Rama divine weapons, including the celestial bow of Lord Vishnu, unbreakable quivers, and a glowing sword. Sage Agastya then directs the royal trio to establish their residence at Panchavati along the banks of the Godavari River.

title: Meeting Jatayu and Establishing Panchavati
story: En route to Panchavati, Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita encounter the majestic vulture king Jatayu, a dear friend of King Dasharatha, who offers his friendship and pledges to help guard Sita in the wilderness. Upon reaching the serene banks of the Godavari River, Lakshmana lovingly builds a sturdy and comfortable leaf hut for their residence. Settling into the breathtaking surroundings of Panchavati, the royal trio begins a peaceful life in their new forest home.

title: Encounter with Surpanakha
story: While living peacefully in Panchavati, Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita are approached by the demoness Surpanakha, the sister of Ravana, who becomes captivated by Rama's beauty. After both Rama and Lakshmana reject her romantic advances, an enraged Surpanakha lunges to attack Sita. Protecting Sita, Lakshmana swiftly intervenes and disfigures the demoness by cutting off her nose and ears, setting into motion the central conflict of the epic.

title: The Destruction of Khara and Dushana
story: Humiliated and disfigured, Surpanakha flees to her brother Khara in Janasthana to demand swift vengeance. Enraged, Khara marches upon Panchavati with his general Dushana and a formidable army of fourteen thousand rakshasas. Instructing Lakshmana to guard Sita in a cave, Rama single-handedly confronts and annihilates the entire demon horde, including Khara and Dushana.

title: Surpanakha Incites Ravana
story: Following the total destruction of the demon army in Janasthana, a distraught and disfigured Surpanakha flees to Lanka to inform her brother, King Ravana, of Khara's death. Enraged by the defeat, Ravana listens intently as she vividly describes Sita's peerless beauty and urges him to abduct her as the ultimate vengeance against Rama. Overcome by lust and fury, the ten-headed demon king resolves to kidnap Sita and sets off to seek the help of the sorcerer Maricha.

title: Ravana and Maricha's Conspiracy
story: Ravana arrives at Maricha's hermitage to seek his aid in abducting Sita as revenge against Rama. Maricha urgently warns Ravana of Rama's supreme might and advises against the dangerous plan, but Ravana threatens him with immediate death if he disobeys. Choosing to die at Rama's hands rather than Ravana's, Maricha reluctantly agrees to transform into a golden deer to lure Rama away from Panchavati.

title: The Golden Deer Temptation
story: Maricha assumes the form of an extraordinarily beautiful golden deer adorned with shimmering gems and grazes near the hermitage at Panchavati. Captivated by its magnificent appearance, Sita earnestly begs Rama to capture the magical creature for her. Disregarding Lakshmana's warning that the deer is a demon in disguise, Rama pursues the elusive creature deep into the forest, leaving Lakshmana behind to guard Sita.

title: Maricha's Deceptive Cry
story: Deep in the forest, Rama shoots the golden deer with a lethal arrow, forcing Maricha to revert to his true demon form. As he dies, Maricha mimics Rama's voice and cries out loudly for help to deceive Sita and Lakshmana. Hearing the distressed call, Sita is overcome with fear and compels a reluctant Lakshmana to leave her unprotected and search for Rama.

title: The Abduction of Sita
story: Taking advantage of Sita being left alone, Ravana approaches the Panchavati hermitage disguised as a harmless wandering ascetic begging for alms. Upon revealing his true terrifying form and being met with fierce resistance, the enraged demon king forcefully seizes Sita and drags her onto his golden chariot. Ignoring her frantic cries for Rama and Lakshmana, Ravana takes to the sky, speeding south toward his kingdom of Lanka.

title: Jatayu's Valiant Sacrifice
story: Hearing Sita's distressed cries from the sky, the noble vulture king Jatayu courageously intercepts Ravana to rescue her. A fierce aerial battle ensues in which Jatayu heroically shatters Ravana's golden chariot and disarms the demon king. However, Ravana ultimately severs the ancient bird's wings with his sacred sword, leaving Jatayu mortally wounded on the earth as Ravana continues his flight toward Lanka.

title: Sita's Imprisonment in Lanka
story: Upon arriving in Lanka, Ravana attempts to entice Sita by showcasing his opulent palace and immense power, but she fiercely rejects him and reiterates her devotion to Rama. Enraged by her unyielding refusal, the demon king orders her to be imprisoned in the Ashoka Vatika garden under the strict vigil of fearsome demonesses. Isolated and heartbroken, Sita steadfastly awaits Rama's rescue while enduring the torment of her captors.

title: Rama's Anguish at the Empty Ashram
story: Returning toward Panchavati after slaying Maricha, Rama meets Lakshmana on the path and immediately fears for Sita's safety. Upon reaching their hermitage and finding it desolate and empty, Rama is overcome with profound grief and despair. Heartbroken, he frantically searches the surrounding forest, desperately asking the trees, animals, and rivers if they have seen his beloved wife.

title: Jatayu's Final Message to Rama
story: Continuing their desperate search through the forest, Rama and Lakshmana discover the noble vulture Jatayu lying mortally wounded on the ground. With his dying breath, Jatayu informs Rama that Ravana abducted Sita and fled toward the south, giving the brothers their first vital clue. Heartbroken by the king's selfless sacrifice, Rama lovingly performs Jatayu's funeral rites before continuing their quest.

title: The Encounter with Kabandha
story: As Rama and Lakshmana head further south through the dense wilderness, they are suddenly ensnared by Kabandha, a monstrous demon with a single eye in his chest and immense, reaching arms. The brothers swiftly sever the monster's arms, breaking a ancient curse and releasing a celestial Gandharva who was trapped within the demonic body. In gratitude for his liberation, the divine spirit advises Rama to seek an alliance with the exiled monkey prince Sugriva at Mount Rishyamuka to locate Sita.

title: Shabari's Devotion and Liberation
story: Following Kabandha's advice, Rama and Lakshmana arrive at the hermitage of Shabari, a devout elderly ascetic who has patiently awaited Rama for years. Overwhelmed with joy, Shabari lovingly offers them wild fruits and receives Rama's blessings before shedding her mortal form to attain liberation. Reassured by her deep faith, the brothers continue toward Lake Pampa on their journey to meet Sugriva.

title: The First Meeting with Hanuman
story: As Rama and Lakshmana approach Mount Rishyamuka, the exiled Vanara king Sugriva spots them and fears they are assassins sent by his hostile brother Vali. Sugriva dispatches his wise minister, Hanuman, disguised as a young ascetic, to ascertain the brothers' true identity and intentions. Deeply moved by Rama's eloquent speech and divine presence, Hanuman reveals his true form and vows to unite Rama with Sugriva.

title: The Sacred Alliance with Sugriva
story: Carried upon Hanuman's shoulders to the peak of Mount Rishyamuka, Rama and Lakshmana are warmly introduced to the Vanara prince Sugriva. In the presence of a sacred fire lit by Hanuman, Rama and Sugriva forge an eternal pact of friendship and mutual assistance. Rama promises to slay Sugriva's tyrannical brother Vali and restore Sugriva's kingdom, while Sugriva vows to mobilize his vast forces to locate and rescue Sita.

title: Rama Proves His Might to Sugriva
story: To reassure a hesitant Sugriva of his ability to defeat the formidable Vali, Rama is asked to demonstrate his extraordinary strength. With a single effortless kick, Rama hurls the massive skeleton of the demon Dundubhi miles away, and then shoots an arrow that pierces seven mighty Sal trees, the earth, and the underworld before returning to his quiver. Deeply awed by this display of divine power, Sugriva's doubts are entirely dispelled, and he gains absolute faith in Rama's promise.

title: The First Battle Between Vali and Sugriva
story: Bolstered by Rama's extraordinary display of strength, Sugriva travels to Kishkindha and issues a thunderous challenge to his brother Vali. As a fierce duel erupts between the two, Rama is unable to fire his lethal arrow because the nearly identical brothers are indistinguishable in combat. Severely beaten, a confused Sugriva flees back to Mount Rishyamuka, where Rama explains his hesitation and promises a distinct strategy for their next confrontation.

title: The Garland of Distinction and Tara's Warning
story: To ensure he can distinguish the identical brothers in their next duel, Lakshmana places a flowering Gajapushpi garland around Sugriva's neck before they return to Kishkindha. Hearing Sugriva's renewed, confident challenge, Vali's wise wife Tara senses danger and begs her husband to make peace, warning him of Sugriva's powerful new ally, Rama. Driven by pride and fierce anger, Vali dismisses Tara's pleadings and rushes out to face his brother in their final, fateful conflict.

title: The Slaying of Vali
story: As Vali and Sugriva engage in a fierce second duel, Rama easily identifies Sugriva by the flowering garland around his neck. Positioned behind a tree, Rama fires a deadly arrow that pierces Vali's chest, striking down the formidable Vanara king. As he falls mortally wounded to the earth, a shocked Vali confronts Rama, questioning the righteousness of being struck from concealment.

title: Rama's Discourse on Dharma and Vali's Final Moments
story: Rama responds to Vali's reproaches by explaining that taking his younger brother's wife violated the fundamental laws of Dharma, justifying his divine punishment under royal law. Realizing Rama's righteousness and supreme divinity, a humbled Vali asks for forgiveness and entrusts his son Angada and kingdom to Sugriva's care. With his heart cleansed of malice, the mighty Vanara king breathes his last, leaving Kishkindha in deep sorrow.

title: Vali's Funeral and Sugriva's Coronation
story: Following Vali's tragic death, Tara, Angada, and the Vanaras grieve deeply before conducting the fallen king's funeral rites with full royal honors. Fulfilling his divine pledge, Rama directs Lakshmana to crown Sugriva as the new king of Kishkindha and appoint Angada as the crown prince. With Sugriva established on the throne, Rama and Lakshmana retreat to a cave on Mount Prasravana to wait out the impending monsoon season before resuming the search for Sita.

title: The Monsoon of Sorrow and Sugriva's Neglect
story: During the heavy four-month monsoon season, Rama resides in a cave on Mount Prasravana, deeply grieving and yearning for his lost wife, Sita. Meanwhile, safe inside the luxurious palace of Kishkindha, King Sugriva becomes entirely consumed by worldly pleasures and wine, completely neglecting his sacred promise to mobilize the Vanara army. As the rains finally begin to clear, Rama's sorrow turns into growing anxiety and anger over his ally's apparent betrayal.

title: Lakshmana's Wrath and the Ultimatum
story: Enraged by Sugriva's continued delay and broken promise, Rama dispatches a furious Lakshmana to Kishkindha to deliver a stern ultimatum. Armed with his bow and burning with indignation, Lakshmana marches into the Vanara capital, terrifying the guards and citizens as he prepares to confront the oblivious king.

title: Tara Pacifies Lakshmana and the Vanara Mobilization
story: Sensing the immense danger of Lakshmana's fiery wrath, Queen Tara uses her wisdom and diplomatic grace to soothe his anger, reassuring him of Sugriva's unyielding devotion. Pacified by her soft counsel, Lakshmana forgives the repentant Vanara king, who swiftly orders the mobilization of millions of Vanara warriors from across the world to aid Rama in searching for Sita.

title: The Gathering of the Vanaras and Rama's Ring
story: Accompanied by Lakshmana, a repentant Sugriva presents himself before Rama along with millions of assembled Vanara warriors from across the world. Sugriva organizes his vast army into four groups, dispatching them toward the north, south, east, and west to locate Sita within a strict one-month deadline. Placing special faith in Hanuman, who leads the critical southern search party, Rama entrusts him with his royal signet ring as a token for Sita to recognize him as a true messenger.

title: The Search for Sita and the Enchanted Cave
story: The search parties set out in all four directions, with the crucial southern group led by Angada, Hanuman, and Jambavan thoroughly scouring dense forests and rugged mountains. As the one-month deadline draws dangerously close, the exhausted and parched Vanaras enter a pitch-black subterranean cave belonging to the ascetic Svayamprabha. Moved by their sacred mission to find Sita, Svayamprabha restores their strength with food and water and uses her mystic powers to magically transport them directly to the southern ocean shore.

title: Sampati Reveals Sita's Location
story: Reaching the vast southern ocean, Angada and the Vanaras fall into deep despair upon realizing their one-month deadline has expired, resolving to fast unto death. Hearing them honor the heroic sacrifice of Jatayu, Jatayu's elder brother, the giant vulture Sampati, emerges to inquire about his sibling. Deeply moved by their tale, Sampati uses his divine, far-reaching vision to inform the overjoyed search party that Sita is held captive a hundred yojanas across the sea in Ravana's fortress of Lanka.

title: Jambavan Awakens Hanuman's Powers
story: Facing the vast and daunting ocean, the Vanaras fall into despair over who among them possesses the strength to leap a hundred yojanas to Lanka. The wise elder Jambavan approaches Hanuman, reminding him of his divine lineage, matchless power, and latent abilities forgotten due to a childhood curse. Inspired by Jambavan's stirring speech, Hanuman realizes his immense capability and expands into a colossal form atop Mount Mahendra, ready to leap across the sea.

title: Hanuman's Epic Leap Across the Ocean
story: Launching himself from Mount Mahendra with monumental force, Hanuman leaps across the vast ocean toward Lanka, overcoming a series of divine tests and demonic obstacles. He gracefully declines the restful hospitality of Mount Mainaka, outsmarts the snake-mother Surasa, and slays the shadow-capturing demoness Simhika. Victorious over all perils, Hanuman successfully lands on the shores of Lanka, taking his first steps into Ravana's formidable realm.

title: Hanuman Infiltrates Lanka and Defeats Lankini
story: To infiltrate Ravana's heavily guarded fortress unnoticed, Hanuman shrinks his colossal form to the size of a small cat and approaches the city gates at nightfall. He is challenged by Lankini, the fierce demonic guardian deity of Lanka, who attacks him for attempting to enter without permission. Hanuman strikes her down with a single blow, fulfilling a divine prophecy of Lanka's eventual ruin and prompting Lankini to bless his sacred quest and grant him entry.

title: Hanuman Searches the Palaces of Lanka
story: Concealed under the cover of night, Hanuman wanders through the magnificent, golden city of Lanka, meticulously searching every mansion, court, and alley for Sita. He infiltrates Ravana's opulent palace and marvels at the divine aerial chariot Pushpaka Vimana, even briefly mistaking Queen Mandodari for Sita before realizing Rama's virtuous wife would never dwell in such lavish comfort. Determined to complete his mission despite his growing anxiety, Hanuman prepares to search the one remaining sanctuary: the Ashoka Grove.

title: Hanuman Discovers Sita in the Ashoka Grove
story: Entering the serene Ashoka Vatika, Hanuman searches the lush foliage until he spots a deeply sorrowful woman sitting beneath a Simshapa tree, surrounded by menacing demonesses. Observing her radiant purity, profound grief, and unwavering devotion to Rama despite her emaciated state, Hanuman realizes with boundless joy that he has finally found Sita. Perched invisibly among the branches above, he sheds tears of relief and carefully considers how to approach her without causing alarm.

title: Ravana Confronts Sita in the Ashoka Grove
story: As Hanuman watches silently from the branches above, Ravana enters the Ashoka Vatika surrounded by attendants to coerce Sita into becoming his queen. Sita fearlessly rejects his advances, placing a humble blade of grass between them and boldly declaring her absolute loyalty to Lord Rama. Enraged by her defiance, Ravana gives her a two-month deadline to submit to him before leaving her to be harassed by the surrounding demonesses.

title: Trijata's Prophetic Dream and Hanuman's Comfort
story: As the demonesses harshly torment Sita following Ravana's departure, the virtuous demoness Trijata intervenes by recounting a vivid, prophetic dream predicting Lord Rama's glorious victory and Ravana's total ruin. Once the guards drift off to sleep, Hanuman softly begins singing the noble deeds and virtues of Lord Rama from the treetop, soothing Sita's anguish and preparing to reveal his presence.

title: Hanuman Presents Rama's Signet Ring to Sita
story: Descending humbly from the tree, Hanuman approaches Sita and reveals himself as a messenger sent by Lord Rama. Though initially suspicious that he might be Ravana in disguise, Sita's doubts are completely dispelled when Hanuman presents Rama's sacred signet ring as proof of his identity. Overwhelmed with emotion and restored hope, Sita sheds tears of joy, blesses Hanuman, and accepts him as Rama's true ally.

title: Sita Entrusts the Chudamani to Hanuman
story: Sita entrusts Hanuman with her precious crest-jewel, the Chudamani, as a sacred token of her love to present to Lord Rama. Though Hanuman offers to carry her back across the ocean immediately, Sita gracefully declines, insisting that Rama himself must defeat Ravana to restore his honor and her dignity. She imparts a poignant message and private memories for Rama, urging Hanuman to hasten her rescue before time runs out.

title: Hanuman Ravages the Ashoka Grove
story: Having fulfilled his divine mission to locate Sita and receive her crest-jewel, Hanuman decides to assess Lanka's defenses and test the strength of Ravana's forces before departing. Assuming a colossal form, he begins uprooting the grand trees and demolishing the royal structures of the Ashoka Vatika, carefully sparing only the tree sheltering Sita. Terrorized by his overwhelming power, the surviving demoness guards flee in panic to alert King Ravana of the mysterious creature wreaking havoc.

title: Hanuman Defeats Lanka's Champions and Prince Aksha
story: Infuriated by the devastation of the Ashoka Vatika, Ravana dispatches thousands of demon guards, fierce commanders, and eventually his brave young son, Akshayakumara, to destroy the intruder. Displaying extraordinary strength and agility, Hanuman single-handedly annihilates the demon armies and slays Prince Aksha in a fierce aerial combat. Stunned by the tragic loss of his son and finest warriors, a deeply shaken Ravana realizes the severity of the threat and prepares to deploy his most powerful warrior, Indrajit.

title: Indrajit Binds Hanuman with the Brahmastra
story: Enraged by the death of his son Aksha, Ravana sends his invincible elder son, Indrajit, to capture the formidable intruder. Following an intense battle of divine weaponry, Indrajit discharges the supreme weapon, the Brahmastra, which successfully immobilizes Hanuman. Showing deep reverence for Lord Brahma, Hanuman chooses not to break the divine bond and willingly allows himself to be bound so he can be brought directly before King Ravana.

title: Hanuman Confronts Ravana in His Royal Court
story: Bound and brought before King Ravana, Hanuman stands fearlessly in the grand royal court of Lanka. He boldly declares himself as the messenger of Lord Rama and King Sugriva, demanding the immediate and honorable return of Sita. Hanuman sternly warns the demon king that failing to repent will bring absolute ruin upon his kingdom and the complete annihilation of the rakshasa race.

title: Ravana Orders Hanuman's Tail Set Ablaze
story: Furious at Hanuman's bold defiance, Ravana orders the envoy's immediate execution, but his righteous brother Vibhishana intervenes by reminding him that killing a messenger violates sacred law. Reluctantly yielding to Vibhishana's counsel, Ravana instead commands that Hanuman's tail be wrapped in oil-soaked rags and set on fire to humiliate him. The demon guards bind Hanuman's tail with immense lengths of cloth and ignite it, unaware that the brave vanara is preparing to turn their punishment into Lanka's ultimate destruction.

title: Hanuman Sets Lanka on Fire
story: Hanuman breaks free of his bonds and leaps from rooftop to rooftop with his burning tail. Much of Lanka goes up in flames, yet Sita in the Ashoka grove and Vibhishana's house remain untouched.

title: Hanuman Returns Across the Ocean
story: After cooling his tail in the sea and bowing once more to Sita in his mind, Hanuman leaps back over the ocean. The waiting vanaras cheer when he lands and announces that Sita has been found.

title: The Vanaras Plunder Madhuvana
story: Angad and the vanaras, overjoyed, enter Sugriva's guarded honey grove and drink the honey. Dadhimukha complains to Sugriva, who understands from their joy that the mission has succeeded.

title: Hanuman Tells Rama: I Have Seen Sita
story: Hanuman reports to Rama and gives him Sita's Chudamani. Rama presses the jewel to his heart, overcome with emotion, and thanks Hanuman with a tearful embrace.

title: Rama's Army Marches to the Southern Ocean
story: Rama, Lakshmana and the vast vanara army march south to the seashore. Facing the endless ocean, they wonder how such an army could ever cross to Lanka.

title: Vibhishana Leaves Ravana's Court
story: Vibhishana urges Ravana to return Sita and avoid destruction, but Ravana insults him and drives him away. Vibhishana leaves Lanka with a few companions and flies toward Rama.

title: Rama Welcomes Vibhishana
story: Sugriva doubts Vibhishana, but Rama declares that he never refuses one who comes seeking refuge. Rama accepts Vibhishana and promises him the kingdom of Lanka.

title: Rama Prays to the Ocean
story: For three days Rama sits in prayer on the shore asking the ocean for a path, but Samudra does not appear. Rama grows angry, lifts his mighty bow and prepares a fiery arrow.

title: Samudra Appears and the Bridge Begins
story: Terrified, the ocean god appears and bows before Rama. He advises that Nala, the son of Vishwakarma, can build a bridge, and the vanaras begin carrying rocks and trees.

title: The Little Squirrel Who Helped Rama
story: According to popular tradition, a tiny squirrel rolled in the sand and shook it into the gaps of the bridge. Rama smiled and stroked its back lovingly, and it is said that the stripes on squirrels are the marks of his fingers.

title: Rama Spares Ravana's Spies
story: Ravana's spies Shuka and Sarana, disguised as vanaras, are caught in Rama's camp. Rama refuses to harm them, shows them his whole army and sends them back unharmed.

title: Angad Challenges Ravana's Court
story: Rama sends Angad as his messenger to Ravana's court. Angad plants his foot firmly on the floor and challenges the demons to move it, but no warrior in Lanka can.

title: Indrajit Binds Rama and Lakshmana
story: Hidden from sight, Indrajit shoots the serpent arrows of the Nagapasha and binds Rama and Lakshmana. The vanaras despair until Garuda, the king of birds, arrives and frees them.

title: Hanuman and Nila Crush Lanka's Generals
story: In fierce battle Hanuman kills the demon general Dhumraksha, and Nila defeats the mighty Prahasta. The vanara army roars as Lanka's great commanders fall.

title: Rama Spares Ravana: Go and Rest
story: Ravana duels Rama, and Rama strikes down his crown and weapons. Seeing Ravana helpless, Rama tells him to go home, rest and return to fight another day.

title: Ravana Awakens Kumbhakarna
story: Ravana orders his giant brother Kumbhakarna to be woken from his long sleep. The demons use drums, elephants and mountains of food to rouse the mighty giant.

title: The Fall of Kumbhakarna
story: Kumbhakarna warns Ravana that he is wrong, yet marches to war out of loyalty to his brother. He fights with terrifying strength against the vanaras until Rama's arrow ends his life.

title: Ravana's Sons Fall in Battle
story: Devantaka, Narantaka and Atikaya, the sons of Ravana, ride out with terrible weapons. One by one they fall to Hanuman, Angad and Lakshmana.

title: Indrajit and the Illusion of Sita
story: Indrajit creates an illusion of Sita and pretends to kill her before the vanaras' eyes. Hanuman is heartbroken and Rama collapses in grief, until Vibhishana reveals it is only magic.

title: Lakshmana Slays Indrajit
story: Vibhishana tells Lakshmana that Indrajit is performing a secret fire ritual at Nikumbhila. Lakshmana disrupts it and defeats the greatest warrior of Lanka in a mighty duel.

title: Mandodari Warns Ravana
story: Heartbroken at the death of his sons, Ravana prepares to fight to the end. Queen Mandodari begs him to return Sita and make peace, but Ravana will not listen.

title: Ravana's Shakti Strikes Lakshmana
story: In the great battle, Ravana hurls a blazing divine spear, the Shakti, at Lakshmana. Lakshmana falls unconscious, and Rama is devastated by the sight of his beloved brother.

title: Hanuman Brings the Sanjeevani Mountain
story: The physician Sushena says Lakshmana can be saved only by herbs from the distant Himalayas. Hanuman flies there, cannot tell the herbs apart, and lifts the entire mountain to Lanka.

title: The Final Duel: Rama and Ravana
story: Indra sends his divine chariot with Matali as charioteer for Rama. Rama and Ravana begin the final duel as the earth and sky tremble.

title: Agastya Teaches Rama the Aditya Hridayam
story: As Rama grows weary, Sage Agastya arrives and teaches him the Aditya Hridayam, a hymn to the Sun. Rama chants it with full faith, and new strength and courage fill him.

title: The Fall of Ravana
story: Ravana's heads grow back each time they are cut off. Following Vibhishana's hint, Rama fires the Brahmastra at Ravana's navel, and the ten-headed king finally falls.

title: Mandodari's Lament and Vibhishana's Coronation
story: Mandodari mourns over Ravana, and Rama asks Vibhishana to perform his brother's last rites with honour. Rama then crowns Vibhishana as the king of Lanka.

title: Hanuman Brings the News to Sita
story: Hanuman goes to the Ashoka grove and tells Sita that Rama has won. Sita is overjoyed, and the demonesses who guarded her bow down in fear and shame.

title: Sita's Agni Pariksha
story: Sita is brought to Rama after her long imprisonment. To prove her purity before the world, Sita enters the fire, and Agni, the fire god, brings her out unharmed and presents her to Rama.

title: The Gods Bless Rama
story: Brahma, Shiva and the gods appear to praise Rama. The spirit of Dasharatha also appears in the sky, blesses his son and Sita, and Indra revives the vanaras who fell in battle.

title: The Pushpaka Vimana Flight Home
story: Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and the vanaras board Ravana's flying Pushpaka Vimana. As they fly to Ayodhya, Rama shows Sita the ocean, the bridge, Kishkindha and Panchavati.

title: Hanuman Reaches Bharata First
story: The fourteen years of exile are ending, and Rama sends Hanuman ahead to tell Bharata. Hanuman finds Bharata living like an ascetic at Nandigram, still worshipping Rama's sandals.

title: The Reunion of Rama and Bharata
story: Bharata runs to Rama, falls at his feet and returns the sandals he guarded for fourteen years. Rama lifts him up in a long, tearful embrace and the whole of Ayodhya rejoices.

title: Rama's Coronation in Ayodhya
story: Ayodhya is lit with countless lamps as Rama and Sita return. Sage Vasishtha crowns Rama king, and Ram Rajya, a golden age of justice and peace, begins.

title: Hanuman Shows Rama in His Heart
story: At the coronation Sita gives Hanuman a precious pearl necklace. Hanuman bites each pearl looking for Rama's name inside, and when people laugh, he tears open his chest to reveal Rama and Sita in his heart.
